Temporary Electric ServiceTerms and Conditions
Generator-supported temporary power, delivered, connected, commissioned and removed by NCN Electric Inc. | Effective upon customer acceptance

SERVICE PROMISE  One accountable electrical contractor for delivery, one Standard Connection, startup testing, basic handoff, disconnection and pickup - with equipment availability bundled into the quoted Temporary Electric Service.

IMPORTANT CONTRACT NOTICE. These Terms allocate responsibility for high-value equipment, fuel, temporary electrical work, site safety, interruption risk, insurance, indemnity and emergency recovery. The accepted Quote/Service Order, these Terms and any schedules together form the Agreement. A Service Order controls only where it expressly identifies a provision of these Terms that it changes.
1. Agreement; Parties; Commercial Character

“NCN,” “we,” and “us” mean NCN Electric Inc. or the NCN affiliate identified on the Service Order. “Customer” means the person or entity accepting the Agreement and includes its authorized employees, agents, subcontractors and invitees. “Site” is the approved service location. “Equipment” includes each generator, trailer, tank, cable, panel, distribution device, accessory, replacement and related item NCN supplies. “Services” are the delivery, placement, Standard Connection, commissioning, support, disconnection, pickup, fueling and other work stated in the Service Order.

NCN markets the bundled offering as Temporary Electric Service because it combines equipment availability with electrical-contractor services. Customer acknowledges, however, that the Equipment remains NCN property and that risk, tax and insurance treatment depends on the facts and applicable law, not the name of the offering. No title or ownership interest passes to Customer.

Any person signing or electronically accepting the Agreement represents that the person is at least 18 years old and has authority to bind Customer. Delivery, access to the Equipment, energization, payment, or use after receipt of these Terms also constitutes acceptance to the extent permitted by law.
2. Service Order; Scope; Order of Precedence

Each Service Order should identify the Site, service period, Equipment capacity and voltage, included connection, distribution accessories, fuel plan, price, taxes, delivery window, responsible contacts, insurance requirements and any Critical-Load or standby coverage. Customer purchase-order terms do not modify the Agreement and are rejected unless NCN expressly accepts a specific change in a writing signed by an authorized NCN officer.
3. Standard Connection and Excluded Work

Unless the Service Order states otherwise, one “Standard Connection” includes delivery within the quoted service area, placement on a safe accessible surface, pre-start inspection, one connection point using the quoted voltage/phase, standard grounding method, startup, functional testing, basic handoff, disconnection and pickup, with no more than three combined electrician labor hours. NCN controls the means and methods of its electrical work.

The Standard Connection does not include engineering, utility coordination, transfer switches, building modifications, trenching, poles, temporary panels, spider boxes, cable ramps, transformers, long cable runs, multiple connection points, permits, inspections, fire watch, traffic control, crane/forklift work, standby personnel, continuous monitoring or correction of pre-existing conditions unless itemized. These items and delays beyond NCN’s control are Change Work billed at the quoted or then-current rates.
4. Sizing; Customer Information; No Uninterrupted-Power Promise

Customer shall timely provide complete load data, starting currents, duty cycles, voltage, phase, load-growth plans, harmonics/nonlinear loads, sensitive equipment requirements, connection details and site restrictions. NCN may recommend a configuration based on that information, but Customer remains responsible for undisclosed, inaccurate or changed loads.

Temporary Electric Service is not utility-grade, uninterruptible or redundant power. NCN does not guarantee continuous voltage, frequency or operation. Life-safety, healthcare, refrigeration, data, broadcast, ticketed-event and other Critical Loads require a separately designed and quoted redundancy, monitoring, fuel and response plan. Unless expressly included, Customer must maintain its own contingency plan and may not rely on a single unit as the sole protection against loss.
5. Service Period; Billing Time; Metered Use

The “Service Period” begins at the earlier of delivery to the Site or the scheduled delivery time when Customer or the Site is not ready, and ends when NCN physically recovers the Equipment after Customer gives an off-service request and provides unobstructed access. A requested end date is an estimate, not an automatic off-service notice. Customer remains responsible for Equipment and charges until recovery, except that NCN will not add usage charges solely for an unreasonable pickup delay after a documented off-service confirmation when access is available and Customer otherwise complies with the Agreement.
Service day: each consecutive 24-hour period or portion beginning at delivery.
Service week: seven consecutive days.
Service month: 28 consecutive days.
Included use: 10 engine hours per service day, 50 per service week and 200 per service month, unless the Service Order states otherwise.
Excess use: the published excess-hour rate for each hour over the applicable allowance. Hour-meter and telematics records control absent manifest error.
No credit applies for weather, holidays, weekends, idle time, utility availability or Customer’s decision not to use the service.

Approved extensions are billed at the applicable rate. Holding Equipment beyond the authorized period, preventing pickup, moving it, or continuing use after termination is a material breach and may be billed at 150% of the daily rate plus recovery, labor, transport and other costs.
6. Delivery, Placement, Access and Pickup

Customer shall provide accurate directions, an authorized Site contact, scheduled access, a firm level drained surface, adequate ventilation and clearances, legal truck/trailer access, permits and a path free of overhead/underground hazards. Customer authorizes NCN to rely on any apparent Site representative for delivery and placement instructions. Waiting time, aborted trips, restricted-hour access and re-delivery are chargeable.

Customer shall maintain 24/7 emergency access and reasonable scheduled access for inspection, service, fueling, meter reads, disconnection and pickup. NCN may enter the Site at reasonable times to inspect or recover Equipment, subject to Site safety rules provided in advance.
7. Site Control, Security and Prohibited Conduct

From delivery until recovery, Customer controls the Site and shall protect Equipment from traffic, water, flood, salt spray, fire, theft, vandalism, tampering and unauthorized persons. Customer shall not sell, sublet, encumber, conceal, move, export, alter, open locked enclosures, bypass safeguards, change settings or allow third-party repair without NCN’s written approval. Equipment may not be used for an unlawful purpose, beyond rated capacity, in a hazardous/classified location, or where exhaust can enter occupied areas unless specifically designed and approved.
8. Electrical Connections and Load Changes

Only NCN or a qualified electrician approved in writing by NCN may connect, disconnect, ground, alter or extend the supplied system. Customer shall not add or transfer load without approval. Unauthorized connections or load changes void any performance commitment and make resulting calls, damage and interruption Customer-caused. Customer is responsible for its downstream distribution and utilization equipment except to the extent expressly included in NCN’s scope.
9. Operation; Daily Care; Alarms

Only trained, competent and authorized adults may interact with Equipment controls. Customer shall follow posted instructions and laws, keep access doors closed, maintain ventilation, and conduct/document daily visual checks of fuel, leaks, damage, alarms and operating condition. Where instructed, Customer shall record oil/coolant levels and meter hours. Customer must immediately stop use, secure the area and contact NCN for a leak, fire, unsafe condition, abnormal noise, repeated trip, warning light, damage or malfunction. Customer may not continue operation if doing so could cause injury or damage.
10. Fueling Service and Fuel Responsibility

The Service Order will select Customer-Managed Fuel, Scheduled NCN Fueling, On-Call NCN Fueling or Return Refill. Unless stated otherwise, units arrive with a full tank and must be recoverable with a full tank. NCN fueling is a convenience and equipment-support service, not a guarantee against run-out.
Price: documented NCN delivered fuel cost plus the stated per-gallon service margin, plus any disclosed trip/minimum, after-hours, standby, remote-area, tax or third-party charge.
Measurement: generator gauge, tank reading, delivery ticket, telematics or metered gallons may be used; NCN’s documented measurement controls absent manifest error.
Access: Customer must provide timely safe access and an authorized adult when required. A failed delivery or wait caused by Customer is chargeable.

Fuel standard: only the manufacturer-approved grade (normally clean ultra-low-sulfur diesel) may be used. Customer may not use gasoline, water-contaminated fuel, unauthorized additives or dyed fuel where prohibited.
Run-outs and contamination: priming, filters, pumps, injectors, tank cleaning, disposal, spill response, downtime and service calls caused by Customer-managed fuel are chargeable.

Customer shall comply with fire, environmental and spill rules; maintain required extinguishers and clearances; stop the engine when directed; and immediately report any release. Customer is responsible for spills and contamination caused by Customer, its fuel vendor or Site conditions. NCN remains responsible for a release to the extent caused by NCN’s negligent fueling operations.
11. Maintenance; NCN Service Access

NCN performs scheduled maintenance and authorized repairs. Customer shall provide access at manufacturer-recommended intervals and shall not obstruct or delay service. NCN may temporarily stop or de-energize Equipment when reasonably necessary for safety, inspection or maintenance. Customer-caused calls - including run-out, overload, altered connection, blocked ventilation, impact, contamination or unauthorized relocation - are billed at current labor, travel, parts and transport rates.
12. Breakdown; Exclusive Service Remedy

Customer shall promptly report a suspected failure and stop use when instructed. For a failure not caused by Customer, NCN will use commercially reasonable efforts to repair or, if available, substitute reasonably comparable Equipment. If NCN cannot restore service within a commercially reasonable period, Customer’s exclusive monetary remedy is a prorated credit of the affected base service charge from verified loss of service until restoration or termination. No credit applies while NCN lacks access, Customer is in default, or the cause is outside NCN’s scope. Substitute equipment may differ in brand or configuration but should provide materially similar capacity.
13. Rates; Additional Charges; Taxes

Customer shall pay all quoted service, delivery, pickup, mileage, fuel, labor, material, permit, tax, excess-hour, standby, cleaning, damage, loss, recovery and Change Work charges. Rates exclude taxes unless expressly stated. NCN may correct manifest clerical errors. Estimates are not caps unless expressly identified as a fixed price. Customer must provide exemption documentation before invoicing.
14. Reservation, Payment, Card Authorization and Credit

New customers and event/venue customers owe a 50% reservation payment; the balance is due three business days before delivery. Orders placed within three business days require payment in full. A reservation is not firm until NCN receives required payment, acceptance and insurance. Approved commercial accounts follow their written credit terms.

Customer authorizes NCN’s compliant payment processor to charge the payment method on file for amounts due under the Agreement, including extensions, excess hours, fuel, Change Work, failed trips, cleaning, loss and documented damage, with an itemized receipt. NCN may place a reasonable authorization hold. Past-due amounts accrue 1.5% per month or the maximum lawful rate, whichever is less. Customer shall pay reasonable collection costs and attorneys’ fees to the extent permitted by law and shall pay undisputed amounts without setoff.
15. Cancellation, Rescheduling and Weather
More than 14 days before scheduled delivery: refund less 10% of the total Service Order, or full account credit valid 12 months.

Four to 14 days before delivery: the 50% reservation payment is nonrefundable but may be transferred once to a rescheduled date within 12 months, subject to availability and then-current pricing; excess payments are refunded.
Within 72 hours, after dispatch, or after procurement/setup work begins: the full contracted amount is due.

Weather request received by noon on the business day before delivery: NCN may issue a one-time 12-month account credit, excluding committed third-party and nonrecoverable costs. No weather credit applies after dispatch, delivery or setup.

NCN may delay, suspend, disconnect or cancel when Site, weather, road or electrical conditions are unsafe. If NCN cancels before delivery for a reason within its reasonable control, Customer’s remedy is refund of amounts paid for the undelivered scope.
16. Loss, Theft, Damage, Cleaning and Casualty

Customer bears risk of loss, theft, vandalism and physical damage from delivery until NCN recovers and inspects the Equipment, except ordinary wear and tear and damage caused solely by NCN. Customer shall immediately notify NCN, police and its insurer after an incident; protect evidence; secure the Equipment; provide reports; and cooperate with investigation and recovery.

Customer shall pay documented recovery, transport, decontamination, repair or replacement cost; labor and parts; environmental disposal; loss of use during a commercially reasonable repair/replacement period; and diminished value when repair does not restore value, subject to applicable law. “Ordinary wear and tear” excludes damage from overload, impact, water, corrosion, neglect, contamination, misuse, improper fuel, missing parts, unauthorized repair, relocation or failure to perform required daily care.
17. Insurance

Before delivery and throughout the Service Period, Customer shall maintain: (a) commercial general liability of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate; (b) all-risk property/inland-marine coverage for Equipment at full replacement value; (c) workers’ compensation as required by law; and (d) automobile liability of at least $1,000,000 combined single limit when Customer transports or moves any Equipment. NCN may require higher limits based on Equipment value or risk. Policies should name NCN as additional insured for liability and loss payee for Equipment, be primary and noncontributory where available, and provide waiver of subrogation where commercially available. Evidence of insurance does not limit Customer’s obligations.
18. Optional Service Protection

No loss-damage waiver or protection plan is included unless separately described and priced in the Service Order. Customer should not assume its obligations are waived merely because it paid a deposit or service fee.
19. Inspection; Telematics; Photographs and Records

NCN may document condition, fuel and meter readings by inspection, photos, video, delivery tickets and electronic records. Equipment may contain GPS, hour-meter, diagnostic and fuel-monitoring devices. Customer consents to collection and use of location, operating and diagnostic data for dispatch, safety, maintenance, billing, theft prevention, recovery and service improvement, subject to applicable law and NCN’s privacy practices. Customer shall notify its personnel and obtain any legally required consent.
20. Suspension, Default, Termination and Recovery

NCN may immediately suspend, de-energize, terminate or recover Equipment if payment is past due; insurance lapses; Customer breaches the Agreement; the Equipment is moved, seized, threatened, misused or endangered; access is denied; Site conditions are unsafe; or NCN reasonably believes continued service creates risk. Customer shall provide immediate peaceful access and pay resulting recovery costs. NCN may use lawful recovery remedies but will not breach the peace.
21. Emergency and Disaster Recall

NCN may recall, relocate or recover Equipment because of a declared emergency, reasonably anticipated hurricane or disaster, evacuation, safety threat, protection of Equipment, road-access risk or NCN emergency-response obligations. NCN will attempt to give 48 hours’ notice when reasonably possible but may require shorter notice or immediate recovery. Customer shall promptly reduce load, cooperate with safe disconnection and provide access.

NCN will prorate unused prepaid base service charges from disconnection or pickup. Earned mobilization, pickup, labor, fuel and third-party costs are nonrefundable. Recall does not make NCN liable for replacement power, project/event delay, lost revenue or other excluded damages. A non-recallable or priority-reservation product applies only if expressly stated and separately priced.
22. Permits, Compliance and Hazardous Materials

The Service Order will identify permit responsibility. Unless included, Customer is responsible for owner/venue approvals, fire-marshal and environmental requirements, operating permits, noise restrictions, traffic control and third-party fees. Customer shall disclose hazardous/classified locations and regulated materials. Customer may not expose Equipment to asbestos, corrosives, hazardous waste or contamination; if it does, Customer shall stop use and pay lawful testing, decontamination and disposal costs, except to the extent caused by NCN.

TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW, NCN DISCLAIMS IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NON-INFRINGEMENT AS TO EQUIPMENT. NCN WARRANTS ONLY THAT ITS EXPRESSLY INCLUDED ELECTRICAL SERVICES WILL BE PERFORMED IN A PROFESSIONAL AND WORKMANLIKE MANNER CONSISTENT WITH APPLICABLE LICENSING REQUIREMENTS. CUSTOMER’S REMEDIES ARE LIMITED AS PROVIDED IN SECTION 12.

25. Indemnification

To the fullest extent permitted by Florida law, Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless NCN, its affiliates and their officers, employees and agents from third-party claims, losses, fines, liens, damages and reasonable attorneys’ fees arising from Customer’s Site control; inaccurate load/site information; possession, security, operation or fueling of Equipment; unauthorized connection, relocation, alteration or use; Customer’s downstream system; Customer’s breach; or acts of Customer’s personnel, contractors or invitees, but only to the extent not caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of the person seeking indemnity. The duty applies only to the extent enforceable and survives termination.
26. Force Majeure

Neither party is liable for delay caused by events beyond reasonable control, including hurricane, flood, lightning, fire, epidemic, government action, road closure, civil disorder, labor or supply interruption, utility failure, transportation casualty or widespread equipment shortage. Payment obligations for completed work and Customer’s protection of Equipment continue. NCN may allocate scarce resources in a commercially reasonable manner, subject to Section 21.
27. Claims; Governing Law; Venue; Jury Waiver

Customer shall give written notice of a billing dispute within 15 days after invoice and of any other claim within 30 days after discovery, with reasonable detail, without shortening any nonwaivable statutory period. The Agreement is governed by Florida law without regard to conflict principles. Exclusive venue lies in the state or federal courts serving the county of NCN’s principal Florida office, unless the Service Order states another Florida county. TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW, EACH PARTY KNOWINGLY WAIVES TRIAL BY JURY.
28. Notices; Assignment; Subcontractors

Operational notices may be delivered to the contacts in the Service Order by email, text or phone; default, termination and legal notices must also be in writing by email with confirmation, nationally recognized courier or certified mail. Customer may not assign the Agreement or relocate/sublet Equipment without NCN’s written consent. NCN may use qualified subcontractors and remains responsible for its contracted scope.
29. Entire Agreement; Severability; No Waiver; Survival

The Agreement is the complete agreement and supersedes prior discussions about the transaction. Amendments must be in a writing accepted by authorized representatives. Failure to enforce a right is not a waiver. If a provision is unenforceable, it will be modified to the minimum extent necessary or severed, and the remainder continues. Payment, risk, insurance, indemnity, liability, ownership, dispute and data provisions survive. Electronic signatures and records are binding.
30. Customer Acceptance

Customer confirms that it reviewed the Service Order and these Terms, had the opportunity to ask questions and obtain legal/insurance advice, understands that Critical Loads require separate planning, and accepts responsibility allocated by the Agreement.
